episode_title: "More AI Tools Means More Sales"… The Reality of AI in Sales in 2026 | Ep 353

real_qa.q: Why does Gartner report a productivity drop despite increased AI and sales tools adoption?
real_qa.r: Gartner has documented that even with all of these tools available, there is a productivity drop because people are feeling overwhelmed. The issue is that when tools are disparate and scattered across multiple platforms, they consume more time than they save, which contradicts the original goal of investing in these tools to increase productivity.
real_qa.requete: Gartner productivity drop AI sales tools 2026

real_qa.q: What is the true cost comparison between canceling HubSpot and building an internal CRM with employee resources?
real_qa.r: Companies think they can dump their HubSpot subscription costing 80k a year and build internally. However, when employee Sally builds it and spends 80% of her days updating it with feature requests, her 150 grand annual wage means they end up paying 150 grand for a CRM versus the original 80 thousand, causing them to ultimately return to HubSpot or similar platforms.
real_qa.requete: build internal CRM cost versus HubSpot subscription

real_qa.q: How does information fragmentation across multiple tools affect BDR onboarding and ramp time?
real_qa.r: When a team's information is spread across multiple products, SharePoint, and other systems, even team members who work there daily become confused about where data is stored. This information overload significantly impacts BDR ramp time and causes onboarding challenges, as new employees face an overwhelming task of learning where everything is located.
real_qa.requete: BDR onboarding ramp time multiple tools fragmentation

real_qa.q: Why are companies canceling long-term CRM subscriptions and adopting simpler tools in 2026?
real_qa.r: Companies are willing to cancel something they have been on for 10 years, declare data bankruptcy, and abandon overly complex systems because there is just so much unnecessary content in them. They are seeking simpler solutions that actually deliver on the promise of improving productivity rather than adding more overwhelm through additional tool integrations.

real_qa.q: What is the risk of building internal tooling without SOC 2 compliance and data governance?
real_qa.r: Building internal tools introduces significant risks around data sovereignty, data governance, and compliance. When clients ask if internally built tools have SOC 2 certification, it becomes extremely difficult and costly to achieve. This adds substantial hidden complexity and risk that companies building internal alternatives often underestimate.
real_qa.requete: internal tool development SOC 2 compliance risk

real_qa.q: What approach does Recabi take when auditing sales tech stacks to ensure proper diagnosis?
real_qa.r: Recabi conducts objective audits and has actually canceled itself out of deals because after the audit, they determined the client was either not ready for their solution or their current tooling was already working well enough. They prioritize diagnosing the true underlying problem rather than selling solutions, and they point clients to competitors if that better serves their actual needs.
real_qa.requete: Recabi sales tech stack audit methodology
